title: Culture / Subculture Field Model
purpose: Provide a reusable neutral model for Culture, Subculture, Sektur, Farm and lower-field readers without reducing cultures to fixed member lists or labels.

dimensions.question: What repeatedly brings people into relation?
What shared language or symbol system compresses experience?
What behavior gets copied, rewarded, ignored or sanctioned?
What counts as prestige or subcultural capital?
How is a past inherited and corrected?
What technical or institutional systems reproduce the formation?
How can roles, identities and participation change?

distinctions.participation_vs_identification: Participation in a scene does not prove identification with its dominant norms or self-description.
distinctions.centrality_vs_belonging: A target, antagonist or critic can become structurally central without belonging to or endorsing the culture.
distinctions.visibility_vs_authority: Being highly visible does not establish governance power or normative authority.
distinctions.boundary_vs_seal: Subcultural boundaries can be meaningful while remaining porous, overlapping and context-dependent.
distinctions.role_vs_essence: A recurring role is an ecological relation, not a permanent essence of a person.

attention_centrality.definition: A person can be structurally central to a culture's routines, memory and identity without belonging to, endorsing or governing that culture.
indicators: recurring jokes, rituals or references depend on the person
newcomers learn the culture partly through stories about the person
status or expertise is gained through knowledge of the person
archives and commentary repeatedly reactivate the person's role
group identity uses the person as contrast, enemy-image or warning
the scene would lose meaningful content/cohesion if the person disappeared
attention_centrality.boundary: Centrality is not membership, authority, consent or ownership.

reader_purpose: Help a reader move from labels to mechanisms, then from mechanisms to self-location: what the culture teaches, rewards, remembers, punishes, preserves and makes possible.
reader_journey: recognize that the reader is already inside cultural systems
keep culture / subculture / high-control analysis distinct
inspect center, meaning, norms, status, boundary, memory, infrastructure and exit
follow one cultural object through creation, selection, framing, repetition, status, memory, migration, mutation and consequence
identify the reader's own participation through repeating, rewarding, correcting, defending, refusing and exiting
inspect how conflict becomes culturally reproductive
distinguish centrality from membership and target-role from consent
end with agency, repair, role expiry and future generativity

reader_agency.correct: can make accuracy culturally valuable if correction reaches memory
reader_agency.defend: can protect constructively or escalate through humiliation
reader_agency.refuse: declines participation in inherited outrage, ridicule or ritual
reader_agency.exit_return: teaches whether role change and permeability are real

conflict_to_culture.question: What has the conflict begun to reproduce, and who benefits when it continues?

tim_bridge.project_example: Tim can be structurally central to hostile/adversarial cultures without belonging to or endorsing them
tim_bridge.teaching: Tim Dooley thinks culture is what repetition teaches the next person.

reader_exit: what does this culture help people create?
what does it make hard to see?
what does it do with dissent?
what happens to people after they leave?
